bab.ringkasan: Definisi & social function descriptive, struktur identification-description, language features, pola soal karakteristik/kategorisasi/makna frasa — dengan gambar stimulus asli per teks (5 gambar diekstrak ke public/gambar-bing), jodohkan struktur, benar/salah, isian rumpang, dan 25 soal resmi bank (Tristan da Cunha, Svalbard Seed Vault, Great Blue Hole, Cillian Murphy, T-Rex) + pembahasan dua jalur.

sections.teks: Descriptive text explains how a person or an object is like — its form, properties, amount, and others. Social function: to describe, represent, or reveal a person or object, abstract or concrete, so the reader can picture it.

Descriptive adalah teks "potret": tidak ada urutan waktu (itu recount), tidak ada argumen (itu exposition), tidak ada langkah (itu procedure). Soal TKA-nya khas: karakteristik objek, kategorisasi ciri, makna frasa, main idea per paragraf, dan purpose = menggambarkan.

Bayangkan descriptive sebagai sketsa potret: pelukis menyebut subjek dulu (identification), lalu menambahkan detail lapis demi lapis (description) sampai penonton "melihat" tanpa hadir. Setiap detail adalah calon opsi jawaban soal karakteristik.

items: Identification — memperkenalkan & menyatakan subjek/topik utama yang akan dideskripsikan.
Description — merinci subjek (fisik, sifat, jumlah, latar) agar pembaca bisa membayangkannya.

Tristan da Cunha is a remote volcanic archipelago situated in the vast, turbulent waters of the South Atlantic Ocean, thousands of miles away from any continental landmass. As the most isolated inhabited island on Earth, it is defined by its dramatic and formidable geography. The main island is dominated by the towering, symmetrical cone of Queen Mary's Peak, a massive active volcano that often disappears into a thick shroud of mist and low-hanging clouds. The coastline is characterized by sheer, jagged cliffs that plunge directly into the cold, dark depths of the Atlantic, leaving only a small, narrow plateau for human settlement.

The only settlement on the island, known as Edinburgh of the Seven Seas, is a collection of sturdy, brightly painted houses that stand in defiance of the harsh oceanic elements. Life here is governed by the unpredictable rhythms of the sea and the wind, which frequently batter the island with relentless force. There are no airports or luxury resorts; the island is accessible only by a multi-day ship journey from South Africa. The atmosphere is one of profound silence and solitude, broken only by the rhythmic crashing of waves against the volcanic rocks and the cries of indigenous seabirds that call the cliffs their home.

The surrounding environment is a sanctuary of raw, untouched nature, where unique wildlife thrives in total isolation. Because of its remoteness, the island is a vital breeding ground for rare species, such as the Northern Rockhopper penguin and the Atlantic Yellow-nosed albatross. The vegetation consists mainly of hardy ferns and mosses that cling to the rocky soil, creating a lush but rugged green carpet across the slopes. In summer, the landscape is bathed in a soft, ethereal light, while winter brings a monochromatic world of grey seas and snow-capped volcanic peaks, reinforcing its status as a lonely outpost at the edge of the world.

Tristan da Cunha stands as a monumental symbol to the resilience of both nature and the small community that inhabits it. It is a place where time seems to have slowed down, far removed from the frantic pace and digital noise of modern civilization. The island's massive volcanic presence and its location in the middle of a vast watery void create a humbling sense of insignificance for anyone who gazes upon its shores. It remains a mysterious, cold sanctuary—a silent guardian of the South Atlantic that guards its secrets behind miles of impenetrable ocean.

(adapted from https://www.britannica.com/)

opsi: It is located very close to the continental landmass of Africa.
It features luxury resorts and modern airports for easy access.

It is a place where residents can enjoy the digital noise of modern life.

Read the following text carefully!

The Global Seed Vault, located on the remote Norwegian Island of Spitsbergen in the Svalbard archipelago, is a sophisticated facility often referred to as the "Doomsday Vault." It is specifically designed to protect the world's crop diversity from potential natural or man-made disasters. Carved 130 meters deep into a solid sandstone mountain, the vault utilizes the surrounding permafrost to remain naturally frozen year-round. The entrance is a striking, rectangular concrete wedge that protrudes boldly from the snowy mountain face, often illuminated by a glittering light installation that makes it visible for miles across the dark polar landscape.

Inside, the atmosphere is defined by sterile, clinical precision and immense quiet. The facility consists of three large underground chambers, each capable of holding millions of seed samples stored in specialized three-ply foil packages. The internal temperature is strictly maintained at a constant −18 °C to ensure that the seeds remain viable for centuries. The air within the chambers is dry and still, filled only with the faint, rhythmic hum of cooling systems that serve as a crucial backup to the mountain's natural freezing power. It is a sanctuary where the world's agricultural history is preserved in frozen silence.

The environment surrounding the vault is one of the harshest and most remote on Earth. Svalbard is characterized by its barren, icy tundra and a landscape that appears almost extraterrestrial. In winter, the region is plunged into a constant polar night where the sun never rises above the horizon, leaving an endless expanse of white snow and jagged blue ice. The climate is dominated by biting winds and extreme temperatures that frequently drop to −25 °C. This desolate setting, devoid of trees or natural landmarks, provides a formidable natural barrier that enhances the security of the facility.

This deep mountain stronghold serves a critical purpose for the future of global agriculture. Located within the permafrost of a remote Arctic Island, the facility functions as a secure backup for the world's crop diversity. The heavy concrete structure protects millions of seed samples from natural disasters and human conflicts. It provides a sense of security for nations that rely on these biological resources to rebuild their food systems. By holding the history of human farming inside its frozen walls, the vault ensures that the foundations of life remain safe for generations to come.

(adapted from https://thedecisionlab.com)

Which of the following are characteristics of the Svalbard environment mentioned in the text? There is more than one correct answer. Choose all that apply!
opsi: Biting winds and temperatures often drop to −25 °C.
The region experiences a polar night where the sun never rises.
Dense forests and lakes provide a natural barrier for the vault.
The landscape is an endless expanse of white snow and jagged ice.
Polar bears are mentioned as a common sight near the concrete wedge.
ujiPemahaman.pembahasan: Jalur konsep: Berdasarkan teks tersebut, karakteristik lingkungan Svalbard yang disebutkan adalah: Biting winds and temperatures often drop to −25 °C. (Teks secara eksplisit menyatakan bahwa iklim di Svalbard "didominasi oleh angin yang menusuk dan suhu ekstrem yang sering turun hingga −25 °C".) The region experiences a polar night where the sun never rises. (Teks menjelaskan bahwa "pada musim dingin, wilayah ini terjerumus dalam malam kutub yang konstan di mana matahari tidak pernah terbit di atas cakrawala".) The landscape is an endless expanse of white snow and jagged ice. (Teks menggambarkan bahwa malam kutub meninggalkan "hamparan tak berujung dari salju putih dan es biru yang bergerigi", menegaskan karakteristik lanskap Svalbard yang ekstrem.) Jalur Cara Gemilang: Characteristics = adjektiva deskriptif teks (biting winds, permafrost); coret yang tak disebut.

The Great Blue Hole, situated off the coast of Belize, is a colossal submarine sinkhole that serves as a profound testament to the Earth's complex geological history. Characterized by its almost perfect circular shape and deep indigo waters, this natural wonder spans over 300 meters across and reaches a depth of approximately 124 meters. It is nestled within the Lighthouse Reef, a small atoll in the Belize Barrier Reef Reserve System. From an aerial perspective, the stark contrast between the dark blue of the deep hole and the surrounding turquoise shallows creates a breathtaking visual phenomenon that has fascinated explorers and scientists alike for decades.

The formation of the Great Blue Hole dates back to the Quaternary glaciation periods, a time when sea levels were significantly lower than they are today. Originally, it was a terrestrial limestone cave system. Over millennia, percolating rainwater, which became slightly acidic by absorbing carbon dioxide, slowly dissolved the limestone, carving out vast subterranean caverns and elaborate stalactite formations. As the glacial ice melted and sea levels rose during the Holocene epoch, these caverns were inundated with seawater. The increasing weight of the rising ocean, combined with the structural fragility of the eroded limestone, eventually caused the cavern's roof to collapse, leaving behind the vertical chasm that exists today.

Beneath its surface, the Great Blue Hole offers a unique, albeit challenging, environment for marine life and divers. The upper layers are inhabited by various species of sharks, such as the Caribbean reef shark and the hammerhead shark, which navigate the perimeter of the sinkhole. However, as one descends deeper, the environment becomes increasingly inhospitable. At a certain depth, a thick layer of hydrogen sulfide prevents sunlight from penetrating further, resulting in an anoxic zone—a region devoid of oxygen. This lack of oxygen means that the deeper reaches are largely desolate, preserving ancient geological features like massive submerged stalactites in a near-pristine state, undisturbed by biological activity.

Beyond its aesthetic appeal, the Great Blue Hole serves as a crucial "time capsule" for paleoclimatologists. By analyzing the sediment layers and mineral compositions found within the sinkhole, researchers can reconstruct past climate patterns, including historical hurricane frequencies and prolonged periods of drought. These findings provide invaluable insights into how ancient civilizations, such as the Maya, might have been impacted by environmental shifts. Thus, the Great Blue Hole is not merely a destination for adventure. It is a vital scientific site that continues to yield secrets about the planet's atmospheric and geological past.

(adapted from https://whc.unesco.org)

The Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton is a central masterpiece displayed at the Geology Museum in Bandung, West Java. This life-sized replica, donated by the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) in 2000, stands as a massive representation of the most famous predatory dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous period. It is strategically positioned in the History of Life gallery to introduce visitors to the prehistoric world. As the largest dinosaur exhibit in the museum, the skeleton serves as an essential educational tool for students and tourists alike.

The physical structure of the skeleton demonstrates a powerful and formidable predator. It features a large, heavy skull equipped with rows of sharp, serrated teeth designed for crushing bone. The replica stands approximately 6 meters tall and stretches over 12 meters in length, capturing the immense scale of the original 'King of the Tyrant Lizards.' Its sturdy hind legs support the entire weight of the frame, while its famously small two-fingered forelimbs remain tucked near the chest area.

The dynamic posture of the display suggests a sense of motion and dominance. The skeleton is mounted in a walking position with its long, heavy tail balanced perfectly behind the torso to act as a counterweight. Its neck is curved slightly forward, giving the impression that the creature is scanning the gallery for potential prey. This calculated arrangement allows visitors to observe the intricate joints and bone structures from various angles within the exhibition hall.

The educational environment around the skeleton provides deep insights into paleontological history. Interactive displays and informative plaques explain that while the original fossils are kept in the United States, this high-quality cast remains scientifically accurate. The exhibit documents the evolutionary journey of reptiles and the geological timeline when these creatures roamed the Earth. By standing beneath the massive ribcage, guests can truly feel the humbling significance of life that existed millions of years before human civilization.
